units.translation: But Justice sharpens her blade for another deed of harm, on other whetstones, Fate.
But do not cast in my places blood-stained whetstones, harm to young entrails.
sharpening a sword for a man
You will not blunt me, sharpened as I am, with your word.
the seats of ancestral gods and the tombs of forefathers
the shapely tombs of the land of Ilium hold them
highest gods and heavily honored chthonic ones, holding the tombs
a female is the murderer of a male
like a cock near a hen
pity the female and male offspring alike
i.e. female seed. For it concerns the fifty daughters of Danaus.
a race of fifty children – female-sown
an enclitic particle used especially by epic poets for emphasis, meaning roughly the same as the Latin profecto, though this is a somewhat weightier word than the Greek θήν.
Perhaps to be restored. τοὶ δ᾽ ἀνὰ γᾶν Ἀσίαν θὴν οὐκέτι περσονομοῦνται [but they throughout the land of Asia are no longer ruled by Persians]. where δήν [long] is read in M.
You indeed gloss over all the things you want of Zeus.
but they throughout the land of Asia are no longer ruled by Persians

There are no examples of the present: but there are perfect τέθηπα [I am astonished], pluperfect ἐτεθήπειν [I had been astonished] (ἐτεθήπεα [I had been astonished] in Homer), aorist ἔταφον [I was astonished], about which see Thes. vol. 4 p. 365 and Veitch p. 270. ed. tert.
The aorist is read in Aeschylus
I was astonished, I was astonished
I am astonished, pluperfect I had been astonished (I had been astonished
the likeness of a most hateful beast's bite
the manner of a newly caught beast
you pursue a beast in a dream
he has fallen from the nets and the beast is gone
with the milk-loving cubs of wild beasts
for it is not complete to bring ancestral prey to the tents
to hunt, to attain by hunting, to capture
The middle form θηρῶμαι [I hunt] means to hunt
But indeed my son desired to hunt this city
I erred, or I am hunting something like some archer
I hunt the stolen source of fire filled with fennel stalk
that can be caught by hunting, that may be hunted
hunting marriages that are not huntable
Thus Bambergerus for θηρίον [wild beast], a word which the tragedians do not use.
